Baleka Mbete ahead of the SONA

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We hold our breath ahead of the SONA. A diginified affair or once more chaos in the HOUSE?

Summary:
Ten days from now President Zuma will deliver his state of the nation address. But the nation is holding its breath. What will happen? Will the unruly EFF once again begin chanting their now familiar “pay back the money” refrain? Will they insist that the president answers the questions on Nkandla that went unanswered on that day in August 2014 when Parliament descended into chaos? Will South Africans once again see riot police removing MP’s from the house? Will someone pull the live TV feed once again and who gave the order last time?

Further information:
Journalists are lining up for accredition- No more is parliamentary TV the snooze channel, instead its been described as a swashbuckling reality show.

Leading it from the front is once again speaker Baleka Mbete. She has been described as Cruella De Ville who protects President Zuma like a manic lynx. She has been jeered by the opposition and told to go but she has made it clear that she isn’t going anywhere.

Much of what happens in the house depends on the decisions she will make. Recently Baleka has suggested that they will be bending over backwards so that the President will answer questions from the last sitting- but the SONA must go off with dignity and without MP’s raising points of order. She has assured South Africans there will be no disruptions and reading between the lines its clear – Security will be tight and no disruptions will be tolerated

But what of the EFF – will they comply or will their need for drama and disruption once again trump the dignity of parliament. Much has been said about Baleka Mbete and her handling of the explosive situation in parliament last year has been severely criticized. But a new year, heralds a new start. What are her plans for 2015? Will she allow unfettered debate without bias even if it means holding her President to account?

Is she the disgrace her critics allege. Does she hate the truth, detest transparency or abhor debate? Is Parliament just a monumental waste of money, unable to properly debate or find solutions to some of the countries most pressing problems?

In a hard-hitting interview with Bongani Bingwa, Carte Blanche explores these questions and the difficulty of a speaker facing down a mob that nevertheless has legitimate grievances and a right to answers to their questions.

Press Release:


One-on-one with Baleka Mbete
Recent events have seen our parliamentary proceedings described as the most chaotic since the dawn of our democracy. One week away from the State of the Nation Address, Speaker of the National Assembly, Baleka Mbete, gives Carte Blanche a candid one-on-one interview.


Script:


FINAL SCRIPT BALEKA MBETE

Commentary One
When the EFF under the command of enfent terrible Julius Malema sailed into the National assembly in May last year, observers predicted a shake up

Link
The parliamentary Channel was once considered a remedy for insomnia – but that all changed in August last year – the day the EFF demanded that President Zuma pay back the money

Up sound pay back the money

Bongani
Was a line crossed that day?
Baleka
Absolutely

Commentary Two
Since then the speaker of the National Assembly, Baleka Mbete, has been under considerable criticism from the opposition. They say she is biased.

Bongani
What do you say to those that say you protect the president at any cost?
Baleka
I reject that! I work according to the rules and I will continue to do that no matter how much screaming about me protecting this that and the other person

Commentary Three
The parliamentary precinct is currently a hub of activity in preparation for the State of the Nation address.

LINK
On Thursday the President addresses the nation – its supposed to be a dignified affair, but the clock ticking on the EFF website – suggests otherwise

Commentary Four
In a recent warning by Julius Malema he said something different is going to happen there.



Bongani
Is Julius Malema holding a gun to your head?
Baleka
No, not at all, he is not my nightmare, he is a concern beyond the parliament actually.

Bongani
What will you do, if during the president’s speech they disrupt it?
Baleka
We will apply the rules.
Bongani
Will we see the riot police return?
Baleka
You know what, I am not prepared to comment on this matter beyond saying what we envisage and it’s a special occasion unlike any other occasion
Bongani
So are we expecting a showdown?
Baleka
We are not expecting a showdown. We are expecting the president to come and address South Africa.

LINK
Our system of government is founded on the principle of a separation of powers, according to which the president as head of the executive is answerable to parliament, and so when called upon to answer questions he must appear house

Commentary five
But by November despite repeated requests the president had not returned to parliament after that humiliating day in August.

Mmusi Maimane

Where is president Zuma?!

Commentary Five A
The DA staged a protest listing their unanswered questions
Bongani
Why has the president not returned to answer the questions?
Baleka
He is coming in March

Commentary Six
Last year the president couldn’t find time in his diary, she said.

Bongani
Is it not the case that the executive is answerable to you, and must compel the president according to the rules?

Baleka
I don’t know if compelling means go and pick him up and bring him to the house?

Bongani
But if the rules say *** four times- do you not say Mr President you have not met the requirement

Baleka
You know Bongani there are not only rules there are constitutions – who makes those constitutions human beings for their convenience – even in the ANC we have a constitutions but we don’t regard the constitu …we also have to apply our minds and exercise when we want to run away from leadership we point at constitutions we point at rules, you must not regard those things as if they came from heaven.

Up sound
Leave the house
I will not
Up Sound you must go you must go

LINK
As powerful as she is the speaker has an unenviable task – with growing calls for her to go and the house often descending into chaos – she has to have a thick skin

Baleka
I don’t take that personally, these issues must be understood in the context of the political terrain and parliament is that terrain

Bongani
Do you also see the lighter side of statements that you have made?
I refuse to recognize you or you wish? ….

Baleka
Nothing its just that we interact as human beings in the house and when they say you must go what must I do I say you wish!

Commentary Seven
But despite the drama Baleka says they are working together with the opposition to ensure that these shocking scenes from last year are a thing of the past. They are also tightening up the rules

Baleka
We respect one another, there are those that have a particular attitude and we hope that they will grow up and they will mellow
Bongani
Who are you referring to?
I am referring to the people you know
Who are those?
Baleka
Who are very loud, all over the place- nobody needs to introduce them!

THE END

Bongani
